newsitem.title: FRANCE: TENNIS-GRAF ERA ENDED BY COETZER.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-GRAF ERA ENDED BY COETZER.

text.p: Defending champion Steffi Graf failed to reach the last four at the French Open for the first time in more than a decade on Tuesday when she was beaten 6-1 6-4 by South African Amanda Coetzer in the quarter-finals.
Graf, the world number two, has reached the final at Roland Garros eight times in the last 10 years but found herself swept aside by the same opponent who humiliated her 6-0 6-1 in Berlin last month.

Graf, who missed three months of tennis earlier this year with tendinitis in her left knee, never recovered from an abysmal start which allowed Coetzer to reel off the opening four games and take the first set in 34 minutes.

The German, also beaten by Coetzer in the fourth round of the Australian Open in January, did her best to stage a comeback following a rain delay in the second set but ultimately slid to her first defeat in Paris since losing in the 1994 semifinals to Mary Pierce.
Champion at Roland Garros five times in all, including the last two years, Graf may now suffer a further indignity when the new world rankings are released next week.
If Monica Seles defeats Mary Joe Fernandez later on Tuesday, Graf will be ranked below number two in the world for the first time since March 1, 1987.
